rationale: Third and final review round for this diff (schema.sql/schema.replicated.sql widened for 4 views - mv_lines_daily, mv_turns_daily, mv_file_facts_daily, mv_active_time_daily -, two new migration scripts, and every SpanName comparison in cli_analytics_repository.py), now including the staged 'No backfill' rationale comment added to both migration files. The edge-case lens performed an exhaustive full-file re-read of schema.sql, schema.replicated.sql, and cli_analytics_repository.py and found zero remaining claude_code-only SpanName/MetricName comparisons and byte-for-byte consistency between both migration files and their corresponding schema view bodies - returned an empty findings array. The blind lens raised several concerns, all triaged as non-blocking: (1) the deployment-ordering assumption behind the 'no backfill' comment is a documented, deliberate decision (this ships before Cursor ingestion starts) rather than an unaddressed gap, and is not something a ClickHouse script can self-enforce; (2) the 4-file SQL duplication, lack of a migration-tracking mechanism, and lack of a rollback script are accepted tradeoffs from earlier rounds, consistent with this repo having no ClickHouse migration framework at all; (3) ON CLUSTER distributed-DDL completion checking is an operational/runbook concern, not a code defect fixable in this diff; (4) the 'constants defined but not interpolated at every call site' observation is explained by an implementation constraint discovered in round 1 - those query strings use ClickHouse's own {param:Type} client-side binding syntax (plain triple-quoted strings, not Python f-strings), so referencing the Python constants there would require converting to f-strings and escaping every existing placeholder, a materially riskier change for the same outcome; the literal-widening approach taken instead is deliberate. Additionally, this round cross-checked the actual production Cursor-side ingestion code (codemie-code's otlp-dispatcher.js) which confirms cursor.tool/cursor.interaction/cursor.lines_of_code.count span/metric names and their Attributes/type semantics genuinely match what these views assume - resolving the 'unverified Cursor attribute-schema' concern raised (and dismissed on trust) in every prior round with actual verification. One incidental, non-blocking observation: that dispatcher does not currently emit any cursor.active_time.total metric, so mv_active_time_daily's widening is forward-compatible preparation rather than something with live data to route today; harmless, not a defect. No spec/story artifact exists for this change, so confidence is forced low by design (no-spec mode) - this reflects the missing acceptance-criteria audit, not a defect in the code.
